fields.Name: Sales: Forecast by Category
fields.UserQuestion: What are we calling commit, best case and pipeline for this period?
fields.Description: Forecast rollup by ForecastCategoryType (master plan §9.3 measure 3). The three buckets are OVERLAPPING, not a partition — one category normally sets more than one flag, because commit is the floor of the forecast rather than a slice of it. Adding the three columns together produces a meaningless number; they are separate SUMs for that reason.
fields.TechnicalDescription: Grain: Deal. Buckets come from ForecastCategoryType.IncludeInCommit / IncludeInBestCase / IncludeInPipeline — §9.3 says "never a string comparison" and this is that requirement. Dates: open deals placed by ExpectedCloseDate, won deals by ActualCloseDate, same window. UncategorizedOpenCount surfaces open deals with no forecast category rather than dropping them silently.

_comments: PARAMETERS ARE DERIVED BY MJ, NOT DECLARED HERE -- and the authored detail is kept below.
They were declared as relatedEntities['MJ: Query Parameters'], and that made this whole
directory unseedable on a fresh database. MJ derives parameters from the SQL when the query is
created; the declared rows then collided with them on the UNIQUE (QueryID, Name) index -- 18
violations, whole-transaction rollback, 0 of 16 queries landing, byte-identical on a retry.
That was KI-25, and it cost every fresh install its dashboard.
Removing the declarations lets MJ derive them: names and IsRequired come out identical. Type
degrades from date to string on the period parameters, which is harmless here because
QueryForecastSource passes them as ISO date-only STRINGS on purpose -- 'a full timestamp would
invite a query to compare a date column against an instant'. What would genuinely have been
lost is the authored Description and SampleValue, so they are preserved verbatim:
CompanyID (string)
Selling company. Omit for every company. Deal.CompanyID is server-stamped from the pipeline, so it is always present and never needs a fallback.
PipelineID (string)
One pipeline. Omit for all pipelines.
PeriodStart (date)
Inclusive start of the window. Omit for no lower bound.
PeriodEnd (date)
Inclusive end of the window. Omit for no upper bound.
